title: Ask for a gradient
starter:
%x = param [] slot=0 dtype=f32 addrspace=ALU
%w = param [] slot=1 dtype=f32 addrspace=ALU
%t = mul %x %w
%out = %t
hints: You need two changes: a new line that makes the loss, and a different last line.
The loss is `%l = mul %t %t`. `gradient` takes the output first and the input second.
explain: `%out = gradient %l %w` asks how far `%l` moves when `%w` is nudged. With x = 3 and w = 5, `%t` is 15. The last mul sends 15 to each of its operands, and both are `%t`, so `%t` holds 30. `%t` then sends 30 times x, which is 90, to `%w`. Your compiler builds that walk as adds and muls, so the same program gives the right gradient for any x and w.
